'''''Dietes grandiflora''''', commonly named '''fortnight lily''', '''large wild iris''', '''African iris'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sa-venues.com/plant-life/dietes-grandiflora.php|title=African Iris - The Dietes Grandiflora|access-date=16 February 2022}}</ref> or '''fairy iris''', is a [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] perennial [[plant]] of the Iris Family ([[Iridaceae]]) with long, rigid, sword-like green leaves. This species is common in [[horticulture]] in its native [[South Africa]], where it is often used in public gardens, beautification of commercial premises and along roadsides.<ref name=PZA>{{Cite web|last=Turner|first=Sharon|title=Dietes grandiflora DC|date=December 2001|url=http://pza.sanbi.org/dietes-grandiflora|publisher=South African National Biodiversity Institute, South Africa|location=Witwatersrand National Botanical Garden|access-date=16 February 2022}}</ref>

== Description ==
The blooms are white with yellow and violet markings and can be up to four inches (ten cm) in diameter.<ref>{{cite book | last1= Turner | first1= R.J. Jr. | last2= Wasson | first2= Ernie | date= 1999 | title= Botanica | location= not given | publisher= Barnes & Noble | page= 306 | ISBN= 0760716420 }}</ref> Dark markings are found at the base of the outer tepals. These flowers bloom in abundance during summer, especially after rain.{{r|PZA}} They last a couple of days and are followed by 5 cm long green capsules that contain very dark brown seeds, dispersed when the capsule splits open.

==Cultivation==
Plants prefer dappled shade to full sun where they will flower in profusion, though they will grow in shaded areas (with an accompanying loss of flower production). Under favourable conditions, the clumps multiply rapidly. ''Dietes grandiflora'' are drought and frost hardy, making them popular for en masse plantings.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagobotanic.org/plantcollections/plantfinder/dietes_grandiflora--large_wild_iris|title=Dietes grandiflora|access-date=16 February 2022|publisher=Chicago Botanic Garden}}</ref> They are frequently called "Fortnight Lilies" because they typically bloom for two weeks, followed by two weeks of rest.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}}

==Environmental weed==
''Dietes grandiflora'' is considered an "environmental weed" in parts of [[Australia]], particularly [[Western Australia]], [[Queensland]], and [[Lord Howe Island]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/media/Html/dietes_grandiflora.htm|title=Dietes grandiflora|access-date=16 February 2022}}</ref>
